variant.stem_override: A 64-year-old man with a remote history of mediastinal radiation for Hodgkin lymphoma 25 years ago presents with 8 months of progressive exertional dyspnea, fatigue, abdominal distension, and lower-extremity edema. He has stable benign prostatic hyperplasia managed with tamsulosin. Vital signs: BP 110/68 mmHg, HR 88 bpm, RR 18, SpO2 97%. Exam shows JVP at 14 cm H2O with a prominent y-descent, Kussmaul's sign (rise in JVP with inspiration), a pericardial knock on auscultation, hepatomegaly, ascites, and 3+ lower-extremity edema. Lung exam is clear. Echocardiogram shows a normal LVEF, mild biatrial enlargement, septal bounce on real-time imaging, respiratory variation in mitral inflow Doppler (>25%), and an inferior vena cava plethoric without inspiratory collapse. Cardiac CT shows a thickened (6 mm) pericardium with linear pericardial calcification.
variant.rationale_for_variant: A single incidental fact — stable benign prostatic hyperplasia on tamsulosin — was inserted as a distractor. It is unrelated to the constriction-versus-restriction question and supports no answer option, so the correct answer (C) is unchanged.
